findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Moving Init from per-request lazy initialization into NewResourceServer turns every initialization failure (DB connectivity, search index build, watcher setup) into a hard constructor failure that blocks process startup, and no tests in this diff cover constructor-time Init failure paths. Operators running multi-tenant deployments where one tenant's index build fails lose the entire server (or embedded Grafana fails to boot) instead of degrading per-request as before; the deleted per-request Init() guards at Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob have no replacement coverage and the only integration test that exercised this path is skipped (see separate finding).

[BUG] Reordering init so the search index fully builds before initWatcher starts creates a lost-update window: any resource writes committed between the index-build snapshot and the watcher start produce no WrittenEvent for the index, leaving permanently stale search results until a rebuild. Users searching dashboards updated during server startup get stale/missing results indefinitely; the previous order (watcher first, then index build) captured those events. Nothing in the diff addresses catching up from the resource version the index was built at versus the watcher's start position.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds a permanent `t.Skip` for postgres on the only integration test covering the storage server lifecycle (NewResourceServer, which now eagerly runs Init), so the exact behavior this PR changes — constructor-time initialization against a real backend — is verified in CI on no database backend at all (sqlite already skipped, postgres now skipped). A regression in NewResourceServer's eager Init (e.g., the ctx/Init ordering change or the removed per-request guards) ships green in Drone for every DB type; the 'TODO - fix this test' is not tracked to an issue in the diff, so the skip has no removal path.

[ADVISORY] Narrowing the cacheMu critical section in BuildIndex so the map write is the only locked operation leaves the earlier cache read and the entire index build racing: two concurrent build() calls for the same key now both build full indexes and one silently overwrites the other in b.cache. Concurrent first-request index builds (now more likely since Init runs at startup and Search can race getOrCreateIndex across tenants/resources) double the CPU/memory cost of index construction and can publish an index built from a snapshot that another goroutine's build already superseded; the diff contains no test for concurrent BuildIndex for the same key.

[ADVISORY] The new `s.search.TotalDocs()` call in the init success log assumes every search backend implements TotalDocs and returns meaningful data at this point, but no test in the diff asserts the log line or that TotalDocs is safe to call immediately after build completes. If TotalDocs panics or returns zero for file-backed indexes (the bleve file path was just touched in this same PR), the 'search index initialized' success path itself fails after startup completes, converting a log statement into a crash — with the postgres integration test skipped, no automated run would catch it.

[ADVISORY] Moving Init(ctx) from per-request lazy initialization into NewResourceServer converts every former per-request initialization failure (DB unreachable, search index build error) into a hard constructor/startup failure, and blocks process startup on the full search index build. Operators running the unified storage server see the process refuse to start (or the gRPC server never register) when the search backend has a transient error at boot, where previously the server started and only individual requests failed; a slow index build also extends startup time for every deployment.

[BUG] Narrowing the cacheMu critical section from the whole of BuildIndex to just the final cache write allows two concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource to run simultaneously, both calling bleve.New on the same filesystem directory (or both building mem-only indexes) with the loser's cache entry overwriting the winner's. Concurrent requests for the same resource during cache-miss warmup produce two index builds racing on one directory, risking file-lock/corruption errors and wasted duplicate builds; the last writer to b.cache wins while the other index (already handed to callers via builder) leaks. The old code serialized builds for a reason the diff does not trace to any stated performance requirement.

[BUG] The postgres path of the integration test is skipped with a TODO rather than fixed, so the entire storage-server integration coverage that this PR most affects (Init-in-constructor, search init ordering) has zero automated verification on postgres, the primary production database. A regression in NewResourceServer/Init ordering that only manifests on postgres (e.g., index build failure at startup) ships to production undetected; the comment admits it works locally but is disabled in CI, so nobody is running it.

[ADVISORY] Reordering search index initialization before initWatcher changes the event-catchup semantics: the watcher is no longer started until the full search index build completes, widening the window during which writes occurring between snapshot and watcher-start are only captured by the builder's RV-based rebuild, and it is not traceable to any stated requirement in a 'performance optimization' PR. Deployments with large datasets experience a longer window with no watch stream established; any write that lands after the index snapshot but before watcher start depends entirely on the rebuild-from-RV path, and any gap there produces permanently missing search entries until re-init.

[ADVISORY] The deleted `if err == nil` guard's success-path log was removed and replaced with only a TODO comment, so the file-backend branch now emits no log at all on successful index creation, losing operator visibility that the old code provided. Operators debugging index behavior on disk-backed tenants lose the per-directory creation log line; the only trace is the IndexTenants metric counter.

[BUG] NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) eagerly and returns an error, converting what was previously a per-request lazy initialization into a hard startup failure and blocking server construction on the full search index build. A single transient DB error during startup, or a slow/blocked search index build, now prevents the resource server (and the process embedding it) from starting at all; previously the same error only failed individual requests that could be retried, and Create/Read/List could serve traffic while the index was still building. This also turns the search-index build into a startup latency cliff proportional to total document count.

[BUG] The diff reorders initialization so the watcher now starts AFTER the search index is fully built, creating a window where writes committed during index construction are silently never indexed. Any resource created/updated between the moment the index snapshot is taken during build() and the moment initWatcher() subscribes produces no WrittenEvent for the freshly built index (the event fired before the watcher connected), so those documents are permanently missing from search results until a full re-index — previously the watcher was started first so those events were captured.

[BUG] Removing the cacheMu lock held across the whole BuildIndex allows two concurrent callers building an index for the same key to each build a complete index, with the second cache write overwriting the first and any documents indexed into the first instance being lost. Under concurrent getOrCreateIndex for the same NamespacedResource (e.g. two simultaneous first-time Search requests), both goroutines build full indexes; the loser's cache entry is overwritten, discarding writes that flowed into it and doubling peak memory/CPU during the build of large tenants. The prior code serialized builds precisely to prevent this.

[ADVISORY] The only end-to-end integration test of the storage server is now skipped for both sqlite3 and postgres, leaving the eager-init startup path this diff introduces completely untested in CI. The TODO'd skip ('test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally') means CI goes green on a build that may fail to boot the resource server against the primary production database — exactly the path this diff changed most (Init moved into the constructor) is the one no longer exercised; regressions ship undetected.

[BUG] Moving s.Init(ctx) into NewResourceServer converts a per-request failure into a hard constructor failure, changing the deployment contract of the resource server. Any embedding of the unified storage server where the search index or backend init fails (e.g. corrupt bleve index dir, DB temporarily unavailable at boot) now crashes/exits the whole Grafana process at startup instead of returning errors per request as before — this behavioral contract change was made in a PR titled 'performance optimizations' with no stated intent to change failure semantics.

[ADVISORY] All lazy Init guards (Create, Update, Delete, Read, List, Watch, Search, History, Origin, IsHealthy, PutBlob, GetBlob) were removed, but Init retains sync.Once-style self-checking, so any out-of-tree caller who constructs a server without NewResourceServer (tests, alternate constructors) now hits an uninitialized server. Callers that build the struct directly or bypass the new constructor call race into requests on an uninitialized server (nil search index, no watcher) where previously Init was guaranteed on first request; anyone extending this file must now know initialization is a constructor-only responsibility.

[ADVISORY] Init order was silently flipped from watcher-before-search to search-before-watcher, changing which events are guaranteed indexed. Previously the watcher started before search index init; now the search index fully builds first and the watcher starts after, so events written during the (potentially long, seconds+) index build are only captured if the build reads current state after those writes; any gap causes silently stale search results, an intent change made without acknowledgment.

[ADVISORY] The postgres integration test is skipped with a TODO ('test not working with postgres in Drone') rather than fixed, disabling the only CI coverage of this server against the production-likely database. The entire eager-Init refactor in this PR is untested against postgres in CI; a postgres-specific init failure now surfaces only as a hard startup crash in real deployments, and the skip was accepted as part of a 'performance' PR rather than a deliberate test-infra decision.

[ADVISORY] BuildIndex no longer holds cacheMu for the duration of the build, changing the locking contract from 'serialized builds' to 'concurrent builds with only the final cache store locked'. Concurrent callers building the same NamespacedResource key now each build a full index and race to store it in b.cache; the last writer wins and earlier callers' returned indexes are orphaned (for file-backed indexes, also racing to create/write the same directory), a semantic change from the previous mutual exclusion that the diff presents as pure performance work.

[BUG] The only test change in this PR disables the sole integration test for the storage server on postgres with a TODO instead of fixing it, so the PR's central behavioral change (moving s.Init from every request handler into NewResourceServer, making init failure a hard construction/startup error and reordering search-index init before watcher init) now has zero verification on the primary production database backend. CI goes green for postgres while the new Init-in-constructor path and the init-ordering change (search.init before initWatcher, and the bleve BuildIndex critical-section shrink) are completely unexercised; any regression — e.g. NewResourceServer now returning an error that previously surfaced lazily per-request, breaking server startup in Drone — is exactly the failure mode this test existed to catch and it is now skipped with only 'works locally' as evidence. Checked: pkg/server/module_server_test.go is the only test-shaped file in this diff and it only adds the skip; no other spec references NewResourceServer, Init, or BuildIndex.

[ADVISORY] Moving s.Init(ctx) into NewResourceServer converts a previously per-request, retryable initialization into a hard constructor failure that aborts startup. Operators running multi-node Grafana: any transient failure during index building or watcher initialization (e.g., slow DB, bleve directory lock, network blip) that previously failed one request and retried on the next now prevents the resource server (and the process embedding it) from starting at all, turning a partial degradation into a full outage across the fleet on restart.

[ADVISORY] The integration test for the storage server is skipped for postgres with a TODO, leaving the new constructor-time Init path untested against the database backend the production deployments use. The exact change in this PR (Init invoked eagerly inside NewResourceServer, with all per-request Init calls removed) has zero integration coverage on postgres; a regression in the eager initialization path ships undetected until it fails startup in a postgres deployment.

[ADVISORY] Removing the cacheMu lock from the body of BuildIndex and only locking around the final cache assignment allows two concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource to both call bleve.New on the same on-disk directory. During rolling restarts or concurrent index rebuilds of large tenants (size > FileThreshold), two goroutines open the same file-backed bleve index at the same path simultaneously; one of the resulting indexes is discarded from the cache while its on-disk directory remains, and concurrent writes to the same bleve directory can leave a corrupted/partial index that later builds must rebuild from scratch — an availability and disk-state issue, not just a perf nit.

goldens.comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

Whether this is a concrete bug depends on the existence of callers that bypass `NewResourceServer` (not shown in the diff), but the behavioral/API risk is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Init order was silently flipped from watcher-before-search to search-before-watcher, changing which events are guaranteed indexed. Previously the watcher started before search index init; now the search index fully builds first and the watcher starts after, so events written during the (potentially long, seconds+) index build are only captured if the build reads current state after those writes; any gap causes silently stale search results, an intent change made without acknowledgment.

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably flips init order in `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go` `Init()`: previously watcher start ran before `s.search.init(ctx)`, now `s.search.init(ctx)` runs first and `s.initWatcher()` is called after (see the moved block around lines ~294-316). That is an intentional behavior change that could affect whether writes occurring during a potentially long index build are observed via the watcher, but the diff alone doesn’t prove a concrete missed-event bug (it depends on how the index build and watcher interact). It is, however, a specific, diff-grounded correctness/consistency risk that should be acknowledged/validated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The postgres integration test is skipped with a TODO ('test not working with postgres in Drone') rather than fixed, disabling the only CI coverage of this server against the production-likely database. The entire eager-Init refactor in this PR is untested against postgres in CI; a postgres-specific init failure now surfaces only as a hard startup crash in real deployments, and the skip was accepted as part of a 'performance' PR rather than a deliberate test-infra decision.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a TODO skip for `dbType == "postgres"` in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer`, citing it fails in Drone. In the same PR, `NewResourceServer` now eagerly calls `s.Init(ctx)` and many RPC handlers no longer call `Init`, changing when/where init failures surface. With postgres coverage skipped in CI by this diff, these init-path changes are no longer exercised against postgres in that integration test, which is a concrete, diff-grounded test/coverage risk rather than a directly verifiable runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] BuildIndex no longer holds cacheMu for the duration of the build, changing the locking contract from 'serialized builds' to 'concurrent builds with only the final cache store locked'. Concurrent callers building the same NamespacedResource key now each build a full index and race to store it in b.cache; the last writer wins and earlier callers' returned indexes are orphaned (for file-backed indexes, also racing to create/write the same directory), a semantic change from the previous mutual exclusion that the diff presents as pure performance work.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex removed the cacheMu lock that previously covered the entire build (deleted Lock/Unlock at function start) and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. That is a real, diff-grounded semantic change: concurrent BuildIndex callers are no longer serialized and can concurrently execute the index creation/build steps for the same `key` (including `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` for the same directory path) before racing to store into `b.cache`. The diff doesn’t show any other per-key dedup/locking to preserve the prior ‘single builder’ behavior, so this is a concrete concurrency/behavioral concern even if it may have been intended as a perf improvement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The only test change in this PR disables the sole integration test for the storage server on postgres with a TODO instead of fixing it, so the PR's central behavioral change (moving s.Init from every request handler into NewResourceServer, making init failure a hard construction/startup error and reordering search-index init before watcher init) now has zero verification on the primary production database backend. CI goes green for postgres while the new Init-in-constructor path and the init-ordering change (search.init before initWatcher, and the bleve BuildIndex critical-section shrink) are completely unexercised; any regression — e.g. NewResourceServer now returning an error that previously surfaced lazily per-request, breaking server startup in Drone — is exactly the failure mode this test existed to catch and it is now skipped with only 'works locally' as evidence. Checked: pkg/server/module_server_test.go is the only test-shaped file in this diff and it only adds the skip; no other spec references NewResourceServer, Init, or BuildIndex.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a postgres-specific `t.Skip` with a TODO in `pkg/server/module_server_test.go`, and no other test changes are shown. Meanwhile, `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error on init failure, and all per-request `s.Init(ctx)` calls were removed; `Init` also reorders search initialization before starting the watcher, and `bleveBackend.BuildIndex` reduces its lock scope. Skipping the postgres run of this integration test removes CI verification for these nontrivial startup/initialization behavior changes on postgres, which is a concrete, diff-grounded review concern (though not itself a functional defect in production code).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Moving s.Init(ctx) into NewResourceServer converts a previously per-request, retryable initialization into a hard constructor failure that aborts startup. Operators running multi-node Grafana: any transient failure during index building or watcher initialization (e.g., slow DB, bleve directory lock, network blip) that previously failed one request and retried on the next now prevents the resource server (and the process embedding it) from starting at all, turning a partial degradation into a full outage across the fleet on restart.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does move initialization earlier (NewResourceServer now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error), but the finding’s core claim that init used to be “per-request, retryable” is not supported: `server.Init` is guarded by `s.initOnce.Do(...)`, so after the first call it will never retry, and any transient failure would stick and all subsequent requests would keep failing too. The diff changes *when* init happens (constructor vs first request), not a retryable→non-retryable model as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The integration test for the storage server is skipped for postgres with a TODO, leaving the new constructor-time Init path untested against the database backend the production deployments use. The exact change in this PR (Init invoked eagerly inside NewResourceServer, with all per-request Init calls removed) has zero integration coverage on postgres; a regression in the eager initialization path ships undetected until it fails startup in a postgres deployment.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a postgres skip in the integration test (`TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` now calls `t.Skip` when `dbType == "postgres"` with a TODO). In the same PR, `NewResourceServer` now eagerly calls `s.Init(ctx)` and all per-request `s.Init(ctx)` calls are removed from methods like `Create`, `Update`, `Delete`, `Read`, `List`, `Watch`, `Search`, etc. This means the newly introduced constructor-time initialization behavior is not exercised by that integration test on postgres, reducing coverage of the exact changed initialization path on the production-relevant backend. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test/coverage gap rather than a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Removing the cacheMu lock from the body of BuildIndex and only locking around the final cache assignment allows two concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource to both call bleve.New on the same on-disk directory. During rolling restarts or concurrent index rebuilds of large tenants (size > FileThreshold), two goroutines open the same file-backed bleve index at the same path simultaneously; one of the resulting indexes is discarded from the cache while its on-disk directory remains, and concurrent writes to the same bleve directory can leave a corrupted/partial index that later builds must rebuild from scratch — an availability and disk-state issue, not just a perf nit.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for the entire function body and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. For file-backed indexes (size > FileThreshold), the directory path is deterministically derived from `key` (`filepath.Join(b.opts.Root, key.Namespace, fmt.Sprintf("%s.%s", ...))`). With the broad lock removed, two concurrent calls to BuildIndex for the same `key` can both execute `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` on the same on-disk directory at the same time, with no diff-shown per-key synchronization. That can lead to two independent index instances writing to the same directory and only one being stored in the cache, creating a real risk of on-disk index inconsistency/corruption and wasted work.
